name: The Strata Runs (Cross-Tier Freerun Circuit)
description: The Strata Runs are unsanctioned freerunning races that span multiple tiers of Meridian 88 vertically — beginning in Shelf alleys and ending on Tier 4 corporate plaza rooftops, covering as much as 800 meters of elevation change through a combination of legal transit, illegal maintenance shafts, and open urban terrain. Unlike the Unaugmented League's horizontal circuits, Strata Runs explicitly welcome all augmentation levels but enforce a 'raw weight' rule: competitors must carry a physical pack weighted to their own body mass in salvage material, equalizing the advantage of lightweight skeletal augmentation. The current record holder is a Tier 1 resident named Tomás Devereux-Nwosu, whose run through the Calumet-to-Spire corridor in 2223 took 47 minutes and was broadcast illegally on fourteen Underworld feeds simultaneously.
cultural_impact: Strata Runs have become a potent political symbol, with completing a run interpreted as a literal demonstration that Shelf residents can move through corporate space on their own terms. Several Tier 4 corponations have begun lobbying for harsher trespass enforcement specifically in response to the runs' growing visibility.
key_figures: "The Ledger" (anonymous Underworld broadcaster who archives all runs)
locations: The Hinge maintenance shaft network (Tier 1-3 transition zone)
Vantabloc North Plaza rooftop (Tier 4, finish line for the flagship route)
story_hooks: A Tier 4 corponation has hired a team of augmented security runners to intercept and publicly humiliate the next Strata Run competitor on camera — a calculated attempt to reframe the runs as dangerous rather than political.
The Ledger has gone dark mid-broadcast during a run, and the competitor being followed has not been seen since — other runners are organizing to retrace the route and find out what happened.

A Tier 3 athletic corporation approaches Tomás Devereux-Nwosu with a sponsorship offer that would legitimize the Strata Runs as a commercial sport, and the community is fractured over whether acceptance is opportunity or betrayal.
